chaos.description: The chaos rules of camel-chaos: a rule is one line, the target, the fault and its parameters as name=value, then the options (such as at, rate, from, until) and optionally an expectation

targets.name: route
targets.description: A route id, with * for any characters; one route id (no pattern) for stall and lifecycle. Its exchanges are faulted as they enter: error and delay at the first step of the route, where its error handler applies; to reach the sends and steps of a route, use in= with another target

targets.name: endpoint
targets.description: An endpoint URI pattern, with * for any characters; matched with or without the query parameters, and the // after the scheme does not count (kafka:orders* matches kafka://orders?brokers=b1)

targets.name: component
targets.description: The scheme of the endpoint URIs, with * for any characters (no ':')

targets.name: step
targets.description: A step id (to1, or the id set with id("enrich")), with * for any characters

hooks.name: send
hooks.description: The sends to a matching endpoint (to, toD, wireTap, enrich, recipientList, a ProducerTemplate...), before the producer is called, inside the error handler

hooks.name: reply
hooks.description: The reply of such a send, after the producer succeeded: its side effect happened (only with at=reply)

hooks.name: dlq
hooks.description: The send of the dead letter channel to a matching endpoint (only with at=dlq)

hooks.name: poll
hooks.description: The polls of the scheduled poll consumers of the routes

hooks.name: entry
hooks.description: Each exchange that enters a matching route, once: corrupt changes it before the first step, error and delay act at the first step, inside the error handler of the route

hooks.name: step
hooks.description: Each matching step of a route, right before its processor is called

faults.name: error
faults.description: Fails the send, the poll or the step with an exception (a ChaosException without exception=), or the failure of an HTTP component for status=

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Waits that long first, then fails, as a call that times out; the producer is not called

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body of the HTTP response (needs status=)

parameters.name: exception
parameters.description: The class of the exception: a public Throwable with a public constructor taking a String or none (not an InterruptedException)

parameters.name: header.<name>
parameters.description: A header of the HTTP response, such as header.Retry-After=5 (needs status=)

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The message of the exception (the class needs a constructor taking a String)

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The failure of an HTTP component for this status (not with exception= or message=)

faults.name: delay
faults.description: Waits before the send, the poll or the step, as for a slow endpoint

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: How long to wait, or a range such as 100ms..2s for a draw between the two times (from the seeded sequence of the rule)

faults.name: drop
faults.description: A send that reports success without calling the producer, or a poll that is skipped

faults.name: corrupt
faults.description: Changes the message: its headers, the charset of its body, or its body

parameters.name: header
parameters.description: The headers mode=remove-header removes: a name or a pattern with *, ignoring case (without it every header that is not Camel*)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: headers: the headers that are not Camel* get random values; charset: a text body becomes UTF-16 bytes; truncate: a String, byte[] or stream body ends after half of it; empty: the body becomes empty of its kind (or null); remove-header: removes headers

faults.name: duplicate
faults.description: Sends the message twice, as a sender that delivers a message again; the reply of the second send is the reply of the send

faults.name: lifecycle
faults.description: Suspends, stops or removes the route of a route=<id> target, and brings it back after the duration; repeat= takes it down more than once

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: What to do to the route

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: How long the route stays down (at most camel.chaos.maxDuration)

parameters.name: every
parameters.description: The time from one time the route goes down to the next, longer than duration=

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: How many times to take the route down (needs every= when more than 1)

faults.name: stall
faults.description: Short for lifecycle action=suspend: the route stalls for the duration

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: How long the route stays down (at most camel.chaos.maxDuration)

parameters.name: every
parameters.description: The time from one time the route goes down to the next, longer than duration=

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: How many times to take the route down (needs every= when more than 1)

options.name: at
options.description: Narrows the rule to one hook of its target (reply and dlq are reached only with at=)

options.name: draw
options.description: Draws the random choices of rate= as the rule with this id did with the same seed, so a scenario or a test fails the same messages as a rule added while the application ran

options.name: expect
options.description: An expectation of a route after the rule is added: <route>:<count> (at least that many completed), <route>:<kind><op><count>, a time (<route>:meanTime<=2s) or the messages lost between two routes (<route>-><route>:lost<=0)

options.name: from
options.description: When the rule starts after it is added, such as after the warm-up (+30s or 30s)

options.name: in
options.description: Narrows the sends, replies, polls and steps of the target to a route id, with * for any characters: the route of the exchange, not the routes it calls; with at=poll the route whose consumer polls. Not with route=, stall or lifecycle

options.name: key
options.description: The key of a message for an expectation of duplicates (<route>:duplicates<=0), in the simple language: two messages with the same key are the same message; without it the body is the key

options.name: rate
options.description: How often the rule fires: a probability above 0 and at most 1, every Nth match, or bursts (every match during the first part of each period); without it every match fires

options.name: until
options.description: When the rule ends: a number of matches or a time from its start (at most camel.chaos.maxDuration, its default)

options.name: when
options.description: A condition on the message in the simple language, in quotes: the rule fires only for the messages that meet it, and its rate and until count only those. Not with at=poll, stall or lifecycle; a condition on the body needs stream caching

options.name: within
options.description: The time of the expectation (by default until the rule ends)

kinds.name: completed
kinds.description: The exchanges completed in the route

kinds.name: handled
kinds.description: The exchanges handled by the error handler in the route

kinds.name: failed
kinds.description: The exchanges failed in the route

kinds.name: meanTime
kinds.description: The mean time of the exchanges in the route, from entering it until done, such as meanTime<=2s

kinds.name: maxTime
kinds.description: The longest time of an exchange in the route, from entering it until done, such as maxTime<=5s

kinds.name: lost
kinds.description: The messages completed in the route and not in the next one, such as orders->shipping:lost<=0

kinds.name: duplicates
kinds.description: The messages the route completed a second time (the same body, or the same key=) that no idempotent consumer recognised as a duplicate, such as payment:duplicates<=0

limits.maxDuration: camel.chaos.maxDuration (default 10m): the longest until, delay, after, from, burst period and stall or lifecycle duration
limits.time: a number with a unit (ms, s, m, h, d), also combined as 1m30s; a number alone is milliseconds
limits.quoting: a value with spaces or ; is quoted with " or ' (\", \' and \\ inside quotes)

recipes.title: Returns an error (HTTP status)
recipes.description: An HTTP call fails with a status, as a service that is down (503), overloaded (429) or broken (500) answers. The exchange fails with the exception of the HTTP component, as the real call would
uncovers: An error handler that does not retry, or retries a status that will not change, such as 400 or 404
Redeliveries without a delay, which hit an overloaded service again at once
Messages that are lost instead of reaching the dead letter channel
avoid: The endpoint is not HTTP: use Refuses the connection
To test a timeout: a status comes back at once, use Times out
watch: The redeliveries of the step and the exchanges handled by the error handler
The dead letter channel, and a circuit breaker around the call if there is one

recipes.title: Refuses the connection
recipes.description: The send fails with a ConnectException before anything is sent, as when the service is not running or a firewall blocks it
uncovers: Whether a connection error is retried: that is safe, as nothing reached the other side
Long redelivery delays that hold the consumer while the service is down
A circuit breaker that does not open
avoid: To test an HTTP status from a service that is up: use Returns an error
A local file has no connection: use Fails to write
watch: The redeliveries and the exchanges handled by the error handler
The state of a circuit breaker around the call

recipes.title: Fails to write
recipes.description: The send fails with an IOException before the file is written, as when the disk is full or the directory cannot be written
uncovers: Whether a failed write is retried, and whether the retry writes the file whole
Where the message goes when the file cannot be written: when the file is how the dead letter channel parks the message, it is lost
avoid: A remote system such as FTP or a database: use Refuses the connection
watch: The redeliveries and the exchanges handled by the error handler
The files written, and the messages that are in none of them

recipes.title: Is slow
recipes.description: Each send waits a time within the range before it is made, as a slow service. The exchange then goes on as usual: the cost is time, not errors
uncovers: A consumer that falls behind: the throughput of the route drops and messages wait in front of it
Thread pools that fill up with waiting exchanges
Callers of the route (request/reply) that time out
avoid: To test the timeout of the client: the wait is before the call, so the client's timeout does not fire. Use Times out
On a route started by a timer: the timer waits for the exchange, so there are fewer messages, not more load
watch: The mean, p95 and p99 time of the routes, and their throughput
The exchanges in flight

recipes.title: Times out
recipes.description: The send waits, then fails with a SocketTimeoutException without calling the producer, as a call that times out
uncovers: Whether a timeout is retried, and whether that is safe: in real life the other side may have done the work
How long a message takes when every attempt times out: the wait times the attempts
A consumer that stops taking messages while its threads wait
avoid: A long wait with a high rate: each fault holds a thread for that time
watch: The time of the route and the exchanges in flight
The redeliveries and the dead letter channel

recipes.title: Did the work, then failed
recipes.description: The send is made and succeeds, then the exchange fails, as when the reply is lost. The error handler sends it again, so the other side gets it twice
uncovers: Duplicates: an order booked twice, a payment taken twice
Whether the other side or the route is idempotent, such as with an idempotent consumer or a key the other side checks
avoid: Against a real service where a duplicate costs, such as one that charges or sends mail to people
With a high count: until=1 makes one send fail, which is enough to see one duplicate
watch: What the other side received: two of the same
The redeliveries of the step

recipes.title: Is down for a while
recipes.description: Every send fails during the first part of each period and works for the rest, as a service that goes down and comes back
uncovers: A circuit breaker that opens during the outage and closes after it
Redelivery that gives up before the service is back, so the messages go to the dead letter channel
How long the route needs to catch up after an outage
avoid: An outage longer than all the redeliveries together sends every message in it to the dead letter channel: make sure that is what you want to test
watch: The faults per second: on during the outage, off between
The state of a circuit breaker, and the exchanges handled by the error handler

recipes.title: Arrives corrupt
recipes.description: The messages that enter the route are changed before its first step: random headers, the wrong charset, cut in half or empty
uncovers: Validation that is missing, so a bad message gets deep into the route before it fails
A poison message that is redelivered again and again, instead of going to the dead letter channel
Unmarshal and parse errors that are not handled
avoid: When the body is a stream or a file: the charset and the cut change text and bytes only, so those messages are skipped (see the reasons it skipped)
watch: The errors of the steps that read the body
The messages the rule skipped, and why

recipes.title: Polls fail
recipes.description: The polls of a scheduled poll consumer fail, as when the folder, the server or the database is not reachable. No exchange is made: the consumer polls again on its schedule
uncovers: A consumer without a backoff, which fails every poll and fills the log
A health check that does not show a consumer that cannot poll
avoid: On a consumer that does not poll on a schedule, such as a timer, Kafka or JMS: the rule fires 0 times
watch: The errors and the backoff of the consumer
The log and the health checks
